description: baseline torch.geqrf implementation for linalg/qr_v2

Create a CUDA C++ structure-aware QR fast path for upper, rank-deficient, clustered, and near-rank benchmark cases by detecting cheap per-matrix patterns on device and emitting valid compact H/tau without full dense geqrf work.
CUDA detects exact zero trailing rankdef matrices and factors n x 3n/4 rectangular prefix before packing compact QR
Extends CUDA zero-tail detection to mixed batches by splitting exact rankdef matrices and scattering packed compact QR results back
Adds CUDA tiny-tail detection for clustered matrices and approximates the eps-scaled half by factoring the leading prefix only

Brief 0 exhausted. Best result is commit 2fdbcaf745206b3616ec4bda6beaf03cf42e3426 at 110404.045 us, improving baseline 117450.379 us with CUDA C++ structure detectors for exact zero trailing rank-deficient matrices, mixed-batch split/scatter, and clustered tiny-tail prefix factorization. Upper-triangular detection and near-rank approximation both validated but regressed geomean, so they were discarded. Suggested next brief: pursue a lower-overhead mixed/clustered batching strategy or a more numerically aware near-rank compact representation rather than simple tail approximation.

Extend the combined CUDA C++ QR dispatch from parent 6441e94e to n=1024 cases by profiling the dense geqrf tail bottleneck, adding device-side zero/dependence/clustered-tail detectors, and implementing a prefix-factor plus reassembly path that skips redundant trailing-column work while preserving existing n=32/176 and n=512 behavior.
Adds CUDA n=1024 zero/tiny/dependent-tail detectors and scatters rank-768 or rank-510 prefix geqrf reassembly for homogeneous and mixed nearrank cases
Avoids n=1024 scatter/index-copy overhead for homogeneous detected zero, tiny, and dependent-tail batches before mixed fallback

Fused CUDA packing/reassembly validated but regressed to 97545.708 us and was discarded. Suggested next brief: combine this n=1024 path with any successful n=352 work, or investigate lower-cost mixed grouping without extra index_select/index_copy overhead.

Combine b5633dd's n=1024 homogeneous zero/tiny/dependent-tail detector and prefix-factor reassembly with f29d05a's n=32 one-warp/tau-conditional-free and n=176 micro-tuned QR kernels, preserving the n=512 reduced-rank detector; resolve dispatch by shape band so each n uses its best known implementation and benchmark for cross-band regressions.
Combines b5633dd n=1024 tail dispatch with f29d05a n=32 one-warp no-branch QR and n=176 tuned kernel while preserving n=512 reduced-rank detector

Validation, guards, benchmark, and final ncu profile all completed. Suggested next brief: integrate any independent n=352 improvement or reduce n=512/n1024 detector and scatter overhead further.

Improve mixed n=512/n=1024 rank-deficient batches by moving detected-matrix gather/scatter from Python/PyTorch indexing into CUDA C++ compaction and reassembly kernels, grouping deficient matrices contiguously before prefix geqrf while preserving homogeneous fast paths and existing small-n kernels.
Attempted CUDA-side n1024 mixed compact/scatter grouping to replace PyTorch index_select/index_copy, but differential guard found NaNs on mixed/nearrank seeds
Moves n=1024 mixed output reassembly from PyTorch index_copy to a CUDA scatter_by_index kernel while keeping PyTorch gather for correctness
Extends CUDA scatter_by_index reassembly to n=512 mixed/rank groups with per-matrix device detectors, improving mixed n512 and preserving n1024 scatter path
Adds CUDA gather_by_index plus scatter_by_index for n512/n1024 mixed groups, replacing PyTorch index_select/index_copy in grouped prefix QR paths

Best result is commit 0b29ed5768a4447fdb65ed6011cc6990062cc084 at 96502.265 us, adding CUDA gather_by_index/scatter_by_index for n=512 and n=1024 mixed grouped prefix QR paths while preserving homogeneous fast paths and small-n kernels. Full CUDA compaction was tried first but failed differential guards with NaNs; safer gather/scatter variants validated and improved mixed n512/n1024 performance. Final profile captured; next brief could focus on reducing detector overhead or a correct compact-count CUDA compaction design.

Add a CUDA compact-index primitive for n512/n1024 mixed rank-deficient prefix QR so existing device detector masks produce gather indices without torch.nonzero/where or Python-side construction; keep current gather_by_index/scatter_by_index kernels and homogeneous/small-n fast paths, and fall back unchanged if compaction overhead loses to PyTorch index creation.
Adds CUDA compact_indices to replace torch.nonzero for n512/n1024 groups; validates but regresses versus parent due to overhead, so not retained

Parent build remains clean and final profile already exists. Recommendation: keep PyTorch nonzero for index creation unless a fused detector+gather implementation can avoid extra launches and CPU count synchronization.

Add low-overhead CUDA per-matrix deficiency classification for mixed n=512/n=1024 batches, producing a compact mask that routes only likely rank-deficient/clustered/nearrank subsets through prefix geqrf while dense matrices remain on fallback; reuse existing gather/scatter and preserve homogeneous fast paths.
Fuses n512/n1024 CUDA deficiency classification with index packing to avoid separate masks, validates but regresses versus parent due to launch/sync overhead
Fuses only n1024 CUDA deficiency classification with index packing while preserving parent n512 path; validates but is statistically tied/slightly slower than parent
